ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a schematic map of the location of the Shanghai World Expo site, in which the Huangpu River and the positions on both banks can be seen, and place names such as “Nanpu Bridge,” “Lupu Bridge,” and “Expo Center Pavilion” are marked; there is also a north arrow on the right side, indicating that the location is the Shanghai World Expo site area. Reasoning: The holding period given in the question stem is from early May to late October. Shanghai is located at about 31°N. The formula for noon solar altitude is H=90°-|φ-δ|, where φ is the local latitude and δ is the solar declination. From early May to around the summer solstice on June 22, the direct solar point moves northward, the solar declination increases, and the latitudinal difference between Shanghai and the direct solar point becomes smaller, so the noon solar altitude becomes larger; after the summer solstice to late October, the direct solar point moves southward, and the latitudinal difference between Shanghai and the direct solar point becomes larger, so the noon solar altitude becomes smaller. Therefore, during the whole period, Shanghai's noon solar altitude first became larger and then became smaller.
